```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 130)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
  library(patchwork); library(viridis); library(scales); library(forcats)
  library(knitr); library(sf)
})

# Locate the repo root, so the report knits from either the repo root or src/.
repo <- normalizePath(".", mustWork = FALSE)
if (!dir.exists(file.path(repo, "src"))) repo <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = FALSE)

RES <- params$results_dir
if (!dir.exists(RES)) RES <- file.path(repo, params$results_dir)

# Every table is optional: a chunk whose input is missing says so and moves on,
# the same warn-and-skip convention the Julia analyse scripts use.
have <- function(f) file.exists(file.path(RES, f))
grab <- function(f) if (have(f)) suppressMessages(read_csv(file.path(RES, f),
                                                           show_col_types = FALSE)) else NULL
skip_note <- function(f) cat(sprintf("\n> Missing `%s` in `%s`; this section is skipped.\n\n", f, RES))

cfg      <- grab("config_index.csv")
summ     <- grab("summary_sensitivity.csv")
traces   <- grab("traces.csv")
kpost    <- grab("k_posterior.csv")
metrics  <- grab("metric_summary.csv")
mpairs   <- grab("metric_pairs.csv")
assign   <- grab("cluster_assignments_sensitivity.csv")
ariw     <- grab("cross_config_ari.csv")
mcomp    <- grab("model_comparison.csv")
ppcs     <- grab("ppc_stats.csv")
ppcr     <- grab("ppc_replicates.csv")
ppcp     <- grab("ppc_pointwise.csv")
elpdd    <- grab("elpd_differences.csv")

# Configurations are ordered metric-then-s throughout, so every faceted figure
# and every heatmap reads in the same order.
if (!is.null(cfg)) {
  cfg <- cfg %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("geodesic", "hop", "comm_dist", "log_comm")),
           # For hop, s is a window radius rather than a rate, so its label says so
           # and never shares a colour key with a rate of the same number.
           s_lab  = ifelse(infer_s, "inferred",
                    ifelse(metric == "hop", paste0(s, ifelse(s == 1, " hop", " hops")),
                           format(s, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE))),
           short  = ifelse(infer_s, paste0(metric, " (s inferred)"),
                           paste0(metric, "  s=", s_lab))) %>%
    arrange(metric, infer_s, s)
  CID <- cfg$config_id
  lab_of <- setNames(cfg$short, cfg$config_id)
  as_cid <- function(x) factor(x, levels = CID, labels = lab_of[CID])
}

# Figure heights scale with the number of configurations, so the same report
# reads correctly at --test scale (5 configs) and at full scale (19).
NC <- if (!is.null(cfg)) nrow(cfg) else 12
NM <- if (!is.null(cfg)) length(unique(as.character(cfg$metric))) else 8
fh_stack <- function(per, pad = 2) max(4, per * NC + pad)
fh_grid  <- function(per, ncol, pad = 1.4) max(4, per * ceiling(NC / ncol) + pad)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
map_theme <- theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(),
                   panel.grid = element_blank())

# Municipal polygons for every map in the report.
polys <- NULL
mesh <- list.files(file.path(repo, "data", "cleaned"), pattern = "^malha_uf[0-9]+\\.geojson$",
                   full.names = TRUE)
if (length(mesh) > 0) {
  polys <- tryCatch({
    g <- st_read(mesh[1], quiet = TRUE)
    key <- intersect(c("codarea", "CD_MUN", "code_muni"), names(g))[1]
    if (is.na(key)) NULL else { g$geocode <- as.numeric(as.character(g[[key]])); g }
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}
# Falls back to centroid points if the mesh is unavailable, as map_dengue.R does.
as_map <- function(df) {
  if (!is.null(polys)) left_join(polys, df, by = "geocode")
  else st_as_sf(df, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
}
map_fill <- function(v) if (!is.null(polys)) aes(fill = .data[[v]]) else aes(colour = .data[[v]])
map_geom <- function(v) if (!is.null(polys))
  geom_sf(map_fill(v), colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.05) else geom_sf(map_fill(v), size = 1.1)
```

# What this study varies, and what it holds fixed

The dengue application in `src/run_dengue.jl` fits

$$y_i \mid \rho_k, r_k \sim \text{NegBin}\!\left(\text{mean} = E_i \rho_k,\; \text{size} = r_k\right)$$

to the `r if (!is.null(assign)) length(unique(assign$geocode)) else 399` municipalities
of Paraná, with a ddCRP prior over the partition. That prior has two ingredients
we chose rather than estimated: a **decay scale** `s`, fixed at 0.5, and a
**distance metric**, the great-circle distance between municipality centroids.
This report asks how much of the fitted clustering survives changing them.

The likelihood, the priors on $\rho$ and $r$, the proposal families, the proposal
scales and the random seed are **identical across every configuration below**.
Only the ddCRP prior moves. Anything that changes is therefore attributable to
the prior, not to the sampler.

## The decay scale is a rate, not a length

This is the single easiest thing to read backwards. The package defines

$$\Pr(c_i = j) \;\propto\; \exp(-d_{ij}\, s), \qquad j \neq i,$$

so `s` multiplies the distance. **Larger `s` means faster decay and a more local
prior.** (The hop metric is the one exception: there `s` is a window radius in
hops, described below.) The decay length in kilometres is `D_scale / s`, so `s = 0.5` on
distances rescaled by the 232 km median pairwise separation is a decay length of
about 463 km, and `s = 10` is about 23 km. In the flat limit `s = 0.0001` every
pair has weight within $10^{-4}$ of 1 and the ddCRP degenerates into a plain,
distance-independent CRP. That limit is the natural null: if the clustering at
`s = 0.5` looks like the clustering at `s = 0.0001`, the spatial prior is not
doing any work.

```{r config-table, results = "asis"}
              `what the metric is` = metric_description,
              `s` = ifelse(infer_s, "inferred", format(s, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)),
              `iterations` = n_samples, `burn-in` = burn, `thin` = thin) %>%
    kable(caption = "Every configuration. The sampler is identical throughout.") %>%

}
```

# The data

```{r data-overview, fig.height = 4.4}
if (is.null(assign)) skip_note("cluster_assignments_sensitivity.csv") else {
  d1 <- assign %>% filter(config_id == first(config_id))
  p1 <- ggplot(as_map(d1)) + map_geom("incidence") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "magma", name = "per 100k",
                         labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "magma", name = "per 100k") +
    labs(title = "Observed 2024 dengue incidence") + map_theme
  p2 <- ggplot(d1, aes(incidence)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey30") + scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    labs(title = "Incidence is multi-modal", x = "incidence per 100k", y = "municipalities")
  print(p1 + p2 + plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1)))
}
```

The right-hand panel is why a clustering model is plausible at all: incidence is
not a smooth gradient across the state but sits in distinct bands. The question
the rest of this report answers is whether the ddCRP recovers those bands from
the data, or manufactures them from the prior.

# The distance metrics

Municipalities are areal units, not points, so centroid distance is only one
reasonable prior geometry. Three alternatives are included here, all built from
the queen contiguity graph $A$ (two municipalities are adjacent if their
boundaries touch).

```{r metric-table, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(metrics)) skip_note("metric_summary.csv") else {
  metrics %>%
    transmute(metric, s = ifelse(metric == "hop", as.character(s), ""),
              `what it is` = description,
              `median raw scale` = signif(d_scale, 4),
              `max / median` = round(max_off, 2),
              `pairs inside window` = percent(frac_in_window, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
    kable(caption = sprintf(
      "The contiguity graph has %d edges, mean degree %.2f and diameter %d hops. The geodesic and communicability metrics are rescaled by their own median off-diagonal entry, so a given s means the same decay per median separation under each; the hop rows are 0 / 30 window matrices and s is their radius.",
      metrics$n_edges[1], metrics$mean_degree[1], metrics$graph_diameter[1])) %>%
    print()
}
```

**Communicability.** $G = \exp(A)$ counts walks of every length between two
nodes, discounted by $1/\ell!$, so it is the graph analogue of a diffusion
kernel. Two readings of it appear here. `comm_dist` is the communicability
distance $\xi_{ij} = \sqrt{G_{ii} + G_{jj} - 2G_{ij}}$, a genuine metric that
drops straight into $\exp(-sd)$. `log_comm` is $-\log(G_{ij}/\max G)$, which
makes the ddCRP link weight proportional to $G_{ij}^{\,s}$, the most direct
reading of "use $\exp(A)$ as the kernel".

**Hop windows.** For `hop`, **`s` is the window radius in graph hops**, not a
rate: every municipality within `s` edges of $i$ is an equally likely link
target, and every one beyond is suppressed. Larger `s` is therefore a *less*
local prior, the opposite direction to every other metric. The window is the
whole of the prior's spatial content; a decay rate inside it was dropped
because the inferred concentration $\alpha$ absorbs almost all of it. A link
weight of exactly zero would put $-\infty$ into the log-posterior and NaN into
the Metropolis ratio, so the suppression is a soft floor: in-window pairs have
distance 0 and excluded pairs distance 30 under a kernel rate of 1, making them
$e^{-30} \approx 9\times10^{-14}$ times weaker. The window is effectively hard
while every log-weight stays finite.

## How the metrics relate to one another

```{r metric-pairs, fig.height = 3.6}
if (is.null(mpairs)) skip_note("metric_pairs.csv") else {
  long <- mpairs %>%
    select(geodesic_km, hop, comm_dist, log_comm) %>%
    pivot_longer(-geodesic_km, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(recode(metric, hop = "hop distance (edges)",
                                  comm_dist = "communicability distance",
                                  log_comm = "-log communicability"),
                           levels = c("hop distance (edges)",
                                      "communicability distance", "-log communicability")))
  print(ggplot(long, aes(geodesic_km, value)) +
    geom_hex(bins = 45) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "pairs") +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = "Graph metrics against great-circle distance",
         subtitle = "A sample of 20,000 municipality pairs",
         x = "centroid distance (km)", y = NULL))
}
```

Hop distance tracks kilometres closely, as it must in a state with no islands
and fairly even municipality sizes, but with substantial spread: two
municipalities 100 km apart can be anywhere from 2 to 8 hops away depending on
how finely the intervening land is subdivided. That spread is exactly what makes
the hop metrics a genuinely different prior rather than a reparameterisation.

## What each prior lets one municipality link to

```{r metric-weights, fig.height = 6.5}
if (is.null(mpairs) || is.null(assign) || is.null(metrics)) skip_note("metric_pairs.csv") else {
  # Curitiba is the state capital and sits inland, so its neighbourhood is not
  # truncated by the state boundary; it makes the clearest single illustration.
  d1 <- assign %>% filter(config_id == first(config_id))
  focus <- d1$geocode[which.max(d1$pop)]
  fi <- which(d1$geocode == focus)

  # Rebuild the focal row of each metric from the sampled pair table.
  rows <- mpairs %>%
    filter(i == fi | j == fi) %>%
    mutate(other = ifelse(i == fi, j, i)) %>%
    transmute(other, geodesic, hop, comm_dist, log_comm)

  if (nrow(rows) < 50) {
    cat("\n> The sampled pair table is too sparse for this panel at test scale.\n\n")
  } else {
    w <- rows %>%
      pivot_longer(-other, names_to = "metric", values_to = "d") %>%
      # Rates at s = 0.5; the hop window at s = 3, uniform inside it.
      mutate(weight = ifelse(metric == "hop", ifelse(d <= 3, 1, exp(-30)), exp(-0.5 * d)),
             metric = factor(recode(metric, geodesic = "geodesic",
                                    hop = "hop window, s = 3",
                                    comm_dist = "communicability distance",
                                    log_comm = "-log communicability"),
                             levels = c("geodesic", "hop window, s = 3",
                                        "communicability distance", "-log communicability")),
             geocode = d1$geocode[other])
    md <- w %>% left_join(select(d1, geocode, lat, lon), by = "geocode")
    print(ggplot(md, aes(lon, lat, colour = weight)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.1) +
      geom_point(data = filter(d1, geocode == focus), aes(lon, lat),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
      scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "link weight") +
      facet_wrap(~metric) + coord_quickmap() +
      labs(title = sprintf("Prior link weight from %s at s = 0.5", d1$name[fi]),
           subtitle = "Hop panel at window s = 3. A cross marks the focal municipality; sampled pairs only",
           x = NULL, y = NULL) + map_theme)
  }
}
```

```{r metric-flatness, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(mpairs)) {
  spread <- mpairs %>%
    summarise(across(c(geodesic, hop_scaled, comm_dist, log_comm),
                     ~ quantile(.x, 0.95) - quantile(.x, 0.05)))
  cat(sprintf("
One thing that panel makes plain: **the communicability distance is nearly flat beyond the first ring of neighbours.** Its central 90%% of pairs spans only %.2f in rescaled units, against %.2f for great-circle distance and %.2f for hop distance. The reason is structural: $G_{ii}$ dominates $G_{ij}$ for all but immediate neighbours, so $\\xi_{ij} = \\sqrt{G_{ii} + G_{jj} - 2G_{ij}}$ flattens out almost immediately. Under $\\exp(-sd)$ that makes it behave much like the flat limit, and its fitted $K$ should be read against `s` near zero rather than against the other metrics. `log_comm` does not have this problem, because taking a logarithm restores the dynamic range.
",
    spread$comm_dist, spread$geodesic, spread$hop_scaled))
}
```

# MCMC diagnostics

Everything below is read off chains that were burnt in and thinned before being
written, so no further burn-in is applied here.

```{r diag-table, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(summ)) skip_note("summary_sensitivity.csv") else {
  summ %>%
    mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id)) %>% arrange(cid) %>%
    transmute(`config` = as.character(cid),
              `mean K` = round(mean_K, 2), `mode K` = mode_K, `sd K` = round(std_K, 2),
              `ESS(K)` = round(ess_K), `ESS(logpost)` = round(ess_logpost),
              `ESS rho` = round(med_ess_rho), `ESS r` = round(med_ess_r),
              `birth %` = round(100 * acc_birth, 2), `death %` = round(100 * acc_death, 2),
              `fixed %` = round(100 * acc_fixed, 2),
              `ESJD(K)` = round(esjd_K, 3), `time (s)` = round(total_time)) %>%
    kable(caption = "Mixing and acceptance by configuration.") %>% print()
}
```

```{r diag-flag, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(summ)) {
  bad <- summ %>% filter(ess_K < 50) %>% mutate(cid = as.character(as_cid(config_id)))
  if (nrow(bad) == 0) {
    cat("\nEvery configuration reached ESS(K) of at least 50.\n")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("\n**%d of %d configurations have ESS(K) below 50**, so their posterior of $K$ should be read as indicative rather than converged: %s. Low ESS here is itself informative: it is concentrated in the configurations whose prior makes birth and death moves hardest to accept.\n",
                nrow(bad), nrow(summ), paste(sprintf("`%s` (ESS %.0f)", bad$cid, bad$ess_K), collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```

```{r traces, fig.height = fh_stack(0.95)}
if (is.null(traces)) skip_note("traces.csv") else {
  tl <- traces %>%
    mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id)) %>%
    select(cid, draw, K, logpost, alpha_ddcrp) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(K, logpost, alpha_ddcrp), names_to = "q", values_to = "v") %>%
    mutate(q = recode(q, K = "number of clusters K", logpost = "log posterior",
                      alpha_ddcrp = "ddCRP concentration alpha"))
  print(ggplot(tl, aes(draw, v)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.22, colour = "grey25") +
    facet_grid(cid ~ q, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
    labs(title = "Traces after burn-in and thinning", x = "stored draw", y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 7),
          strip.placement = "outside", axis.text = element_text(size = 6)))
}
```

```{r running-mean, fig.height = 4.4}
if (!is.null(traces)) {
  rm <- traces %>% group_by(config_id) %>% arrange(draw, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(running = cummean(K)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id))
  print(ggplot(rm, aes(draw, running, colour = cid)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "turbo", name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "Running mean of K", subtitle = "A curve still drifting has not converged",
         x = "stored draw", y = "running mean K") +
    theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt")))
}
```

# The posterior of the number of clusters

$K$ is a count, so its posterior is drawn as bars rather than a line.

```{r pk, fig.height = max(4, 2.7 * ceiling(NM / 2))}
if (is.null(kpost)) skip_note("k_posterior.csv") else {
  kp <- kpost %>% left_join(select(cfg, config_id, metric, s, infer_s, s_lab), by = "config_id") %>%
    mutate(s_lab = factor(s_lab, levels = unique(cfg$s_lab[order(cfg$infer_s, cfg$s)])))
  print(ggplot(kp, aes(K, prob, fill = s_lab)) +
    geom_col(position = "identity", alpha = 0.62, width = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", name = "s", end = 0.92) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = "Posterior of K by metric and decay scale",
         x = "number of clusters K", y = "posterior probability"))
}
```

# Sensitivity to the decay scale

```{r s-sweep, fig.height = 5.6}
if (is.null(summ)) skip_note("summary_sensitivity.csv") else {
  g <- summ %>% filter(metric == "geodesic", !infer_s)
  inf <- summ %>% filter(infer_s)
  panel <- function(yv, lab, logy = FALSE) {
    p <- ggplot(g, aes(s_decay, .data[[yv]])) +
      geom_line(colour = "grey55") + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
      scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
      labs(x = "decay scale s (rate)", y = lab)
    if (nrow(inf) == 1)
      p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = inf[[yv]][1], linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick")
    if (logy) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
    p
  }
    g$acc_death_pct <- 100 * g$acc_death
    if (nrow(inf) == 1) inf$acc_death_pct <- 100 * inf$acc_death
  print((panel("mean_K", "mean K") | panel("alpha_post", "posterior mean alpha", TRUE)) /
        (panel("acc_death_pct", "death acceptance (%)") | panel("ess_K", "ESS(K)")) +
    plot_annotation(title = "Great-circle metric: everything against s",
      subtitle = "Larger s is a more local prior. The dashed line is the chain with s inferred."))
}
```

```{r s-sweep-text, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(summ)) {
  g <- summ %>% filter(metric == "geodesic", !infer_s) %>% arrange(s_decay)
  inf <- summ %>% filter(infer_s)
  if (nrow(g) >= 2) {
    cat(sprintf("\nAcross `s` from %s to %s, mean $K$ moves from %.1f to %.1f and the posterior mean of the ddCRP concentration $\\alpha$ from %.2f to %.2f. The two move in opposite directions by construction: a more local prior makes distant links unlikely, so more clusters form, and the self-link weight $\\alpha$ needed to explain them falls.\n",
                format(min(g$s_decay), scientific = FALSE), format(max(g$s_decay), scientific = FALSE),
                g$mean_K[1], g$mean_K[nrow(g)], g$alpha_post[1], g$alpha_post[nrow(g)]))
    if (nrow(inf) == 1)
      cat(sprintf("\nThe chain that infers `s` settles at `s` = %.2f with $\\alpha$ = %.3f and mean $K$ = %.1f, and its death acceptance is %.2f%%. That is the degeneracy `run_dengue.jl` documents: left free, `s` runs towards a strongly local kernel where death moves almost never succeed, which is why the application fixes it.\n",
                  inf$s_post[1], inf$alpha_post[1], inf$mean_K[1], 100 * inf$acc_death[1]))
  }
}
```

# The alternative metrics

```{r alt-metrics, fig.height = 5.6}
if (!is.null(summ)) {
  a <- summ %>% left_join(select(cfg, config_id, s_lab), by = "config_id") %>%
    filter(!infer_s, metric != "hop") %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = setdiff(levels(cfg$metric), "hop")),
           s_lab = factor(s_lab, levels = sort(unique(as.numeric(s_lab)))))
  panel <- function(yv, lab, logy = FALSE) {
    p <- ggplot(a, aes(metric, .data[[yv]], fill = s_lab)) +
      geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single"), width = 0.78) +
      scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", name = "s", end = 0.92) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = lab) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, size = 8))
    if (logy) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
    p
  }
    a$acc_death_pct <- 100 * a$acc_death
  print((panel("mean_K", "mean K") | panel("alpha_post", "posterior mean alpha", TRUE)) /
        (panel("acc_death_pct", "death acceptance (%)") | panel("ess_K", "ESS(K)")) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = "Every rate-based metric, at the shared decay scales"))
}
```

```{r hop-sweep, fig.height = 5.6}
if (!is.null(summ)) {
  h <- summ %>% filter(metric == "hop") %>% arrange(s_decay)
  if (nrow(h) > 0) {
    hp <- function(yv, lab, logy = FALSE) {
      p <- ggplot(h, aes(s_decay, .data[[yv]])) +
        geom_line(colour = "grey55") + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = h$s_decay) +
        labs(x = "hop window radius s (hops)", y = lab)
      if (logy) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
      p
    }
    h$acc_death_pct <- 100 * h$acc_death
    print((hp("mean_K", "mean K") | hp("alpha_post", "posterior mean alpha", TRUE)) /
          (hp("acc_death_pct", "death acceptance (%)") | hp("ess_K", "ESS(K)")) +
      plot_annotation(title = "Hop window: everything against the radius s",
        subtitle = "Larger s admits more link targets, so it is a LESS local prior."))
  }
}
```

```{r alt-metrics-text, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(summ)) {
  a <- summ %>% filter(!infer_s, s_decay == 0.5)
  if (nrow(a) > 1) {
    a <- a %>% arrange(desc(mean_K))
    cat(sprintf("\nAt the shared scale `s = 0.5`, mean $K$ ranges from %.1f under `%s` to %.1f under `%s`.\n",
                a$mean_K[1], a$metric[1], a$mean_K[nrow(a)], a$metric[nrow(a)]))
  }
  h <- summ %>% filter(metric == "hop") %>% arrange(s_decay)
  if (nrow(h) >= 2)
    cat(sprintf("\nThe hop windows are the extreme case. Widening the window from %g to %g hops moves mean $K$ from %.1f to %.1f: restricting links to immediate neighbours forbids the long-range links that let a cluster span the state, so the partition fragments and death moves become very hard to accept.\n",
                h$s_decay[1], h$s_decay[nrow(h)], h$mean_K[1], h$mean_K[nrow(h)]))
}
```

# The fitted partitions

Maps use the **mode partition**: the highest log-posterior draw among those
whose cluster count equals the posterior mode of $K$. The Dahl least-squares
partition is also in the exported table, but it over-fragments here because the
co-clustering signal is weak, and its $K$ would not match the $K$ reported
everywhere else.

```{r mode-maps, fig.height = fh_grid(2.7, 3)}
if (is.null(assign)) skip_note("cluster_assignments_sensitivity.csv") else {
  md <- assign %>% mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id))
  # Cluster labels are arbitrary, so colour by each cluster's fitted incidence
  # instead. That makes panels comparable: the same colour means the same rate.
  md <- md %>% group_by(config_id, cluster_mode) %>%
    mutate(cluster_rate = median(rho_mean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% ungroup()
  sf_md <- as_map(md)
  print(ggplot(sf_md) +
    (if (!is.null(polys)) geom_sf(aes(fill = cluster_rate), colour = NA)
     else geom_sf(aes(colour = cluster_rate), size = 0.7)) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "magma", name = "fitted\nper 100k",
                         labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "magma", name = "fitted\nper 100k") +
    facet_wrap(~cid, ncol = 3) +
    labs(title = "Mode partition, shaded by each cluster's fitted incidence",
         subtitle = "Same colour scale throughout, so panels compare directly") +
    map_theme + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5)))
}
```

```{r cluster-sizes, fig.height = max(4, 0.26 * NC + 2.6)}
if (!is.null(assign)) {
  sz <- assign %>% count(config_id, cluster_mode) %>%
    mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id))
  ks <- sz %>% count(cid, name = "K")
  p1 <- ggplot(ks, aes(fct_rev(cid), K)) + geom_col(fill = "grey30") + coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Clusters in the mode partition", x = NULL, y = "K") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
  p2 <- ggplot(sz, aes(fct_rev(cid), n)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3) + coord_flip() + scale_y_log10() +
    labs(title = "Cluster sizes", x = NULL, y = "municipalities per cluster") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  print(p1 + p2)
}
```

# Do the configurations agree with each other?

This is the question the whole study is built around. There is no ground truth
on real data, so agreement between partitions fitted under genuinely different
priors is what stands in for one. High agreement means the clustering is a
property of the data; low agreement means it is a property of the prior.

```{r ari-heat, fig.height = max(4.5, 0.44 * NC + 2.2)}
if (is.null(ariw)) skip_note("cross_config_ari.csv") else {
  h <- ariw %>% mutate(a = as_cid(config_a), b = as_cid(config_b),
                       lab_col = ifelse(ari > 0.55, "black", "white"))
  print(ggplot(h, aes(a, b, fill = ari)) + geom_tile() +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ari), colour = lab_col), size = 2.1,
              show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), oob = squish, option = "viridis", name = "ARI") +
    labs(title = "Adjusted Rand index between mode partitions", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid = element_blank()))
}
```

```{r ari-text, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(ariw)) {
  off <- ariw %>% filter(config_a != config_b)
  cat(sprintf("\nOff-diagonal ARI runs from %.2f to %.2f, median %.2f. ",
              min(off$ari), max(off$ari), median(off$ari)))
  top <- off %>% slice_max(ari, n = 1)
  bot <- off %>% slice_min(ari, n = 1)
  cat(sprintf("The closest pair is `%s` against `%s` (%.2f); the furthest is `%s` against `%s` (%.2f).\n",
              top$config_a[1], top$config_b[1], top$ari[1],
              bot$config_a[1], bot$config_b[1], bot$ari[1]))
}
```

# Model comparison

WAIC, LPML and PSIS-LOO score how well each fit predicts the observed counts.
They are comparable across configurations here because the likelihood is
identical and only the prior over partitions differs. `k>0.7` counts the
observations whose Pareto-smoothed importance weights are unreliable; a large
count means the LOO column should be read with caution and WAIC or LPML
preferred.

```{r model-comp, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(mcomp)) skip_note("model_comparison.csv") else {
  mc <- mcomp %>% mutate(cid = as.character(as_cid(config_id))) %>% arrange(waic)
  mc %>% transmute(`config` = cid, WAIC = round(waic, 1),
                   `dWAIC` = round(waic - min(waic), 1),
                   `p_WAIC` = round(p_waic, 1), LPML = round(lpml, 1),
                   `elpd_loo` = round(elpd_loo, 1), `k>0.7` = n_bad_k) %>%
    kable(caption = "Predictive scores, best WAIC first.") %>% print()
}
```

```{r model-comp-plot, fig.height = max(3.2, 0.26 * NC + 2)}
if (!is.null(mcomp)) {
  mc <- mcomp %>% mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id), d = waic - min(waic))
  print(ggplot(mc, aes(fct_rev(cid), d)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey30") + coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "WAIC relative to the best configuration", x = NULL,
         y = "WAIC - min(WAIC), lower is better") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)))
}
```

```{r elpd-diff, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(elpdd)) {
  cat("\n> No `elpd_differences.csv` (older runs did not save pointwise scores), so the gaps above have no standard errors.\n\n")
} else {
  best <- mcomp$config_id[which.max(mcomp$elpd_loo)]
  dd <- elpdd %>% filter(config_a == best) %>%
    mutate(cid = as.character(as_cid(config_b))) %>%
    select(cid, criterion, diff, se, z) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = criterion, values_from = c(diff, se, z))
  cat(sprintf("\nThe totals above say nothing about how noisy each gap is. Pointwise contributions do: the standard error of a difference in elpd is $\\sqrt{n\\,\\mathrm{var}(a_i - b_i)}$ over the %d municipalities. Every configuration is compared with the best by LOO, `%s`; a gap of under about two standard errors is not a meaningful preference.\n\n",
              length(unique(assign$geocode)), as.character(as_cid(best))))
  dd %>% arrange(desc(diff_elpd_loo)) %>%
    transmute(`config` = cid,
              `elpd_loo deficit` = round(diff_elpd_loo, 1), `se` = round(se_elpd_loo, 1),
              `in se` = round(z_elpd_loo, 1),
              `elpd_waic deficit` = round(diff_elpd_waic, 1), `se ` = round(se_elpd_waic, 1),
              `LPML deficit` = round(diff_lpml, 1), `se  ` = round(se_lpml, 1)) %>%
    kable(caption = sprintf("Shortfall of each configuration against `%s`, with standard errors. Positive means the best configuration predicts better.",
                            as.character(as_cid(best)))) %>% print()
}
```

# Posterior predictive checks

Each configuration generated `r if (!is.null(ppcp)) format(1000, big.mark = ",") else "1,000"`
replicate datasets from its own posterior. A discrepancy statistic the model
cannot reproduce shows up as a posterior predictive p-value near 0 or 1.

```{r ppc-table, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(ppcs)) skip_note("ppc_stats.csv") else {
  ppcs %>% mutate(cid = as.character(as_cid(config_id))) %>%
    select(config = cid, statistic, observed = T_obs, ppp,
           `replicate median` = q50, `2.5%` = q025, `97.5%` = q975) %>%
    mutate(across(c(observed, `replicate median`, `2.5%`, `97.5%`), ~ signif(.x, 4)),
           ppp = round(ppp, 3),
           misfit = ifelse(ppp < 0.05 | ppp > 0.95, "yes", "")) %>%
    kable(caption = "Posterior predictive p-values. `misfit` flags ppp outside [0.05, 0.95].") %>%
    print()
}
```

```{r ppc-hist, fig.height = fh_stack(0.88)}
if (is.null(ppcr) || is.null(ppcs)) skip_note("ppc_replicates.csv") else {
  rr <- ppcr %>% mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id))
  ob <- ppcs %>% mutate(cid = as_cid(config_id))
  print(ggplot(rr, aes(T_rep)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 34, fill = "grey55") +
    geom_vline(data = ob, aes(xintercept = T_obs), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_grid(cid ~ statistic, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = "Replicate statistics against the observed value (red)",
         x = NULL, y = "replicates") +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, size = 6.5),
          strip.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 6)))
}
```

Moran's I of log incidence is the statistic to watch here, because it is the one
the spatial prior is supposed to control. If the fitted clusters reproduce the
observed spatial autocorrelation, its p-value sits away from the extremes; if a
metric under- or over-smooths, this is where it shows.

```{r pit, fig.height = fh_grid(2.1, 4)}
if (is.null(ppcp)) skip_note("ppc_pointwise.csv") else {
  print(ggplot(mutate(ppcp, cid = as_cid(config_id)), aes(pit)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey35", boundary = 0) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(ppcp) / length(unique(ppcp$config_id)) / 20,
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
    facet_wrap(~cid, ncol = 4) +
    labs(title = "Randomised PIT of each municipality's count",
         subtitle = "A calibrated model gives a flat histogram; the dashed line is uniform",
         x = "PIT", y = "municipalities") +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7)))
}
```

```{r ppc-resid-map, fig.height = 5}
if (!is.null(ppcp) && !is.null(mcomp) && !is.null(assign)) {
  best  <- mcomp$config_id[which.min(mcomp$waic)]
  worst <- mcomp$config_id[which.max(mcomp$waic)]
  rd <- ppcp %>% filter(config_id %in% c(best, worst)) %>%
    left_join(select(filter(assign, config_id == best), geocode, lat, lon), by = "geocode") %>%
    mutate(z = (y_obs - yrep_mean) / pmax(sqrt(pmax(yrep_mean, 1)), 1),
           cid = factor(config_id, levels = c(best, worst),
                        labels = c(paste0("best WAIC: ", best), paste0("worst WAIC: ", worst))))
  print(ggplot(as_map(rd)) +
    (if (!is.null(polys)) geom_sf(aes(fill = z), colour = NA) else geom_sf(aes(colour = z), size = 0.8)) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "grey92", high = "#b2182b",
                         midpoint = 0, name = "std.\nresidual",
                         limits = c(-1, 1) * quantile(abs(rd$z), 0.97, na.rm = TRUE),
                         oob = squish) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "grey92", high = "#b2182b",
                           midpoint = 0, name = "std.\nresidual") +
    facet_wrap(~cid) +
    labs(title = "Standardised posterior predictive residuals",
         subtitle = "Spatial structure left in the residuals is structure the prior did not capture") +
    map_theme + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8)))
}
```

# What to take from this

```{r conclusions, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(summ) && !is.null(ariw)) {
  g <- summ %>% filter(metric == "geodesic", !infer_s) %>% arrange(s_decay)
  off <- ariw %>% filter(config_a != config_b)
  cat(sprintf("
1. **The decay scale changes how many clusters there are, not whether there are any.** Over the full seven-order-of-magnitude grid, mean $K$ runs from %.1f to %.1f. Every configuration finds several clusters, so the multi-cluster finding itself is not an artefact of the chosen `s`.

2. **The flat limit is the informative comparison.** At `s = %s` the kernel is uniform and the model is a plain CRP with no spatial information at all. How far the `s = 0.5` partition sits from that one is the honest measure of what the spatial prior contributes.

3. **The metric matters at least as much as the scale.** Restricting links to a hop window is a much stronger intervention than changing the decay rate at fixed geometry, because it removes the long-range links entirely rather than merely down-weighting them.

4. **Agreement across priors is the correctness check.** Off-diagonal ARI has median %.2f. Read alongside the fact that no ground truth exists here, that is the substantive evidence about how much of the partition the data pins down.
",
    min(g$mean_K), max(g$mean_K), format(min(g$s_decay), scientific = FALSE), median(off$ari)))
}
```

## Caveats

- **Chain length.** These are
  `r if (!is.null(cfg)) format(max(cfg$n_samples), big.mark = ",") else "250,000"`-iteration
  chains (burn-in `r if (!is.null(cfg)) format(max(cfg$burn), big.mark = ",") else "50,000"`,
  thinned by `r if (!is.null(cfg)) max(cfg$thin) else 10`), the same length as the
  headline dengue chains. Configurations flagged above for low ESS should
  still be read as indicative.
- **`s` means two things.** It is a decay rate for the geodesic and
  communicability metrics and a window radius in hops for `hop`, so a value of
  `s` is only comparable within a metric.
- **The truncation floor.** Hop windows suppress rather than forbid distant
  links, at $e^{-30}$ relative weight. That is numerically necessary, since an
  exact zero would put $-\infty$ into the log-posterior, and it is far below any
  weight the sampler can act on, but it is not literally zero.
- **The decay scale is a rate.** Larger `s` means a more local prior. Two places
  in this repository previously described it as `exp(-d/s)` and read the
  direction backwards; that has been corrected, and every number here follows
  the code.
- **The metric-weight panel** is drawn from a 20,000-pair sample rather than the
  full matrix, so it shows the shape of each neighbourhood rather than every
  municipality in it.

```
Rscript src/prepare_dengue_adjacency.R --uf 41
julia --project=. src/dengue_sensitivity.jl --pilot   # measure cost first
julia --project=. src/dengue_sensitivity.jl           # or --slurm
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("src/dengue_sensitivity_analysis.rmd")'
```
